newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat with weak demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat with weak demand.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot product prices flattened late amid lower New York futures and thin local demand, traders said.
Dealers said wholesale prices for West Coast products would be unchanged or drift lower next week, as flooding kept motorists off roads in central and northern California.
Despite upcoming maintenance at several regional refiners, buying dried up this week because weak driving demand caused inventory to build at terminals.
Products for prompt January delivery were seen two cents lower than February supplies, due to weak demand, traders said.
Conventional unleaded in San Francisco shed a half cent from yesterday to 74/75 cents a gallon.
CARB-grade gasoline in the Bay fetched 75.50/76.50 cents a gallon, down a cent from Thursday, as crude futures settled 28 cents lower at $26.09 a barrel.
